documents.title: NOVA Policies and Procedures syllabus insert, Fall 2026
documents.stance_why: The only AI text says AI use to complete assigned work "may be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy" and urges caution with assignment web tools absent "explicit permission" from instructors. It sets no tiers or blanket ban and leaves permission to instructors, but the default is restrictive: AI to complete work is presumptively misconduct unless permitted.
documents.summary: A one-paragraph Academic Integrity section in a college-wide syllabus insert. It warns that using AI to complete assigned work may violate the integrity policy, urges caution with assignment tools without instructor permission, and lists sanctions and Turnitin.

units.why: The sentence says "the use of AI to complete assigned work may be considered a violation of the academic integrity policy". It classes AI use on assignments as potential academic misconduct, so P36; it is hedged ('may'), hence informs, and it binds students.
units.anchor: the use of AI to complete assigned work may be considered a violation

units.why: "Students are urged to be cautious when using any web tools designed to assist with assignments without their instructors' explicit permission" advises care and ties use to instructor permission. It does not ban, so it is closest to P03 (discourage without forbidding); P04 is not chosen because no per-instructor decision procedure is set.
units.anchor: Students are urged to be cautious when using any web tools designed to assist
units.fit_note: Also makes instructors' explicit permission the condition for using such web tools; it does not name AI explicitly.

units.why: "cite their sources in all their work" is a general citation duty attached to the AI/web tool sentence. It is nearest to P24 (acknowledge or cite use), though it does not name AI or a statement.
units.anchor: to cite their sources in all their work
units.fit_note: Generic citation of sources; AI is not named, and no format or statement is specified.

units.why: "Consequences of academic dishonesty can include a failing grade on an assignment, a failing grade in the course" lists concrete sanctions for academic dishonesty, which the document extends to AI use; so P37, though the penalties are 'can include', not fixed.
units.anchor: a failing grade on an assignment, a failing grade in the course
units.frag_end: suspension or expulsion from the college.
units.fit_note: Penalties are for academic dishonesty generally, not AI specifically.

units.why: "NOVA faculty may choose to use tools such as Turnitin to detect and flag instances of plagiarism" permits faculty to use similarity-checking software; P40 covers similarity checking. AI detection is not named.
units.anchor: NOVA faculty may choose to use tools such as Turnitin to detect and flag
units.fit_note: Names plagiarism detection only, not AI detection.

notes: Only one sentence concerns AI explicitly; other units are the surrounding integrity text it relies on. Academic Integrity Policy 224 not read. Spring 2026 insert excluded as superseded.
